topics.title: Space data-centre constellation
topics.summary: US regulators authorised SpaceX's proposed Starmind constellation, a plan for up to one million satellites supporting space-based computing that also raises questions about debris, emissions and astronomy.
topics.discussionPrompt: If computers really moved into orbit, what would amaze you most: the engineering, the solar power, or trying to keep the night sky friendly for stargazers?

topics.title: Smaller Brussels sprouts
topics.summary: Britain's Brussels sprout harvest is reportedly smaller this year after a hot, dry summer affected the water-loving crop, putting a seasonal food detail in the climate conversation.
topics.discussionPrompt: If one holiday side dish had to become the star of dinner, which would you choose: sprouts, potatoes, stuffing, or something completely unexpected?

topics.title: Belgian data-centre pause
topics.summary: Google was told to halt construction on a Belgian data centre over a planning-permit issue, spotlighting how rapidly growing computing projects meet local approval processes.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big new project comes to town, what would you care about first: jobs, environmental impact, design, or whether locals were genuinely heard?

topics.title: A new Brussels museum
topics.summary: Brussels opened a major new museum development in a former Citroen garage, turning a large industrial site into a space for modern and contemporary art.
topics.discussionPrompt: What old building near you would make the best reinvention: a museum, library, indoor garden, music venue, or something else?

topics.title: Working-class songs preserved
topics.summary: A folk singer is helping preserve songs from the Industrial Revolution's working-class communities, bringing old everyday stories to new audiences.
topics.discussionPrompt: What kind of everyday story deserves to become a song: the commute, a favourite local shop, family recipes, or the chaos of group chats?

topics.title: Sharper tide forecasts
topics.summary: New ways of measuring tides could improve flood forecasting, offering communities a more detailed view of changing water levels and coastal risk.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your phone could send one genuinely useful local alert, would you pick flood risk, transit delays, air quality, or the perfect time for a walk?

topics.title: Markets rebound after holiday
topics.summary: US stock indexes rose in a shortened session as investors returned to AI-linked technology shares, ending a volatile week with broad gains.
topics.discussionPrompt: When something bounces back after a rough week, do you see it as a fresh start or a reminder to slow down and look twice?

topics.title: Jobs report watch
topics.summary: Investors are looking toward the next US employment report and central-bank decisions, with technology earnings also expected to shape the mood in markets.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is your personal version of an economic indicator: coffee prices, concert tickets, grocery bills, or whether your favourite shop has a sale?

topics.title: Electrification keeps moving
topics.summary: After COP31 stalled, countries and companies highlighted continued investment in electrification, including expanding power grids and cleaner heavy transport.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which change would you notice most in everyday life: quieter electric buses, more charging spots, cleaner deliveries, or a more reliable local grid?

topics.title: AI helps conservation work
topics.summary: Environmental groups are using AI for tasks such as sorting and translating field notes, while also weighing the energy and land demands of data centres.
topics.discussionPrompt: What repetitive task would you gladly hand to a helpful assistant: sorting photos, planning meals, translating notes, or finding lost files?
